references.text: Rebekah's nurse Deborah died and was buried under the oak below Bethel, which was called Allon-Bachuth (the oak of weeping), showing that places were named after weeping and mourning.
The context for Bokim, where the angel of the Lord spoke to the Israelites and they wept over their disobedience to the covenant.
The Israelites wept before the Lord and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, demonstrating the same pattern of weeping and sacrifice.
The people came to Bethel and wept loudly before the Lord, built an altar, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings.
Jacob named the place Bethel, showing the tradition of naming places based on significant events.
Abram built an altar for the Lord at Bethel, establishing the area as a place of worship.
